quote: Chloe thinks about it for most of her fifteen minutes.
why: states the fact that she thought, for a specific duration, without rendering any of the reasoning itself, so the reader gets a summary of cognition instead of an instance of it.
suggestion: Render the actual deliberation: "Three times the pay anywhere else pays. A degree, already paid for. Stay, and there's no next thing to go and do."

rule_name: Repetition as Emphasis, Say It Once and Let Placement Do the Work
quote: You don't stay at your school. Nobody stays at their school.
why: the same speaker restates one claim twice back to back, second person then generalized, with no new information added by the repeat.
suggestion: Cut the first sentence and keep only "Nobody stays at their school."

rule_name: Dialogue That States the Theme, Cut the Character's Gloss on Their Own Image
quote: that's the whole point of there being a next thing
why: Chloe explains the significance of the line she just said, handing the reader a delivered conclusion instead of letting the preceding image (going and doing the next thing) carry its own meaning.
suggestion: End the line on the image itself: "You go and do the next thing." Cut the trailing gloss entirely.

rule_name: The Said-Bookism Overcorrection, Vary Attribution in Long Exchanges
why: opens a four-turn, two-speaker exchange (lines 172-181) that carries only one dialogue tag, "Kavi says," attached to the final line, so the reader has to count turns to know who is speaking for three lines running, with no physicality anywhere in the passage.
suggestion: Attribute or anchor more of the turns, e.g. "Why?" Chloe says. ... "But it's school," she says, still standing in the doorway. -- so the exchange isn't carried by a single trailing tag.
